thread.title: Apple's shaping up for an earnings beat - and that will push it to $1 trillion, strategist says

author: morningstar.com
title: Apple's shaping up for an earnings beat - and that will push it to $1 trillion, strategist says
text:
By Victor Reklaitis, MarketWatch
Critical information for the U.S. trading day
It's Apple earnings day, and beaten-up bulls are hoping that means it's also "Turnaround Tuesday."
The backdrop isn't exactly that promising, with the Nasdaq having shed nearly 4% over the past three sessions. Morgan Stanley says "the selling has just begun (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/prepare-for-the-biggest-stock-market-selloff-in-months-morgan-stanley-warns-2018-07-30)," and we're even hearing from perma-bear John Hussman, who runs an underperforming fund that has seen massive outflows (https://www.wsj.com/articles/a-stock-permabear-wont-give-in-1504576920?mod=mktw). He warns of a "danger zone (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-prophet-of-doom-predicts-stock-market-will-plunge-more-than-50-2018-07-30)" for the stock market.
But Apple (AAPL)could come to the rescue with its results after the close, suggests our call of the day, which comes from Ken Berman at Gorilla Trades.
"I predict an all-around beat, possibly by as much as $1 billion in sales (over $53 billion), and up to seven cents ($2.26) on per-share earnings," writes Berman (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/today-research-reports-stocks-watch-120000498.html), who is the stock-picking service's founder and CEO.
He predicts the encouraging results will be "driven by a heavier mix of higher-priced iPhones, momentum in iPads and strength in services."
The beat will jolt Apple's stock higher and push the tech giant's market cap above $1 trillion, he adds.
"Apple will be the first company in history to reach this milestone, but others will quickly follow, notably Amazon, then Alphabet, which I forecast will arrive before Microsoft," the strategist says.
Others point out the Colossus of Cupertino could've been a trillionaire long ago (https://www.wsj.com/articles/apple-couldve-been-a-trillionaire-long-ago-1533031200?mod=mktw), but instead it spent big on buybacks and dividends.
Read:Apple earnings -- Brace for hints about the next iPhone (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apple-earnings-most-boring-quarter-of-the-year-still-holds-some-intrigue-2018-07-27)
And see:Earnings Watch -- even Apple takes a back seat to Elon Musk's Tesla right now (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/earnings-watch-even-apple-takes-a-back-seat-to-elon-musk-right-now-2018-07-29)
Also possibly cheering up bulls, Bespoke Investment Group is noting (https://twitter.com/bespokeinvest/status/1024020748514545664) that, if history is any guide, Nasdaq names look set for a rally:
(https://twitter.com/bespokeinvest/status/1024020748514545664)
Key market gauges
Futures for the Dow , S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 are slightly higher, after the Dow , S&P and Nasdaq Composite slumped yesterday (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-stock-futures-dip-putting-sp-500-on-pace-for-3rd-down-session-in-a-row-2018-07-30).
With one day left in July, the Dow is up 4.3% for the month, while the S&P and Naz have tacked on 3.1% and 1.6%, respectively.
Europe is slightly higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-search-for-firm-direction-as-earnings-roll-in-with-inflation-data-in-focus-2018-07-31), after Asia finished mixed (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-mixed-as-investors-wait-on-bank-of-japan-announcement-2018-07-30). Oil and gold are falling, while the dollar index is little changed. Bitcoin is trading back under $8,000.
See the Market Snapshot column (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/nasdaq-set-to-stabilize-after-three-session-skid-2018-07-31) for more.
The chart
Love for motorcycles -- is it an every-other-generation thing? That's the story told by the Daily Shot (https://blogs.wsj.com/dailyshot/2018/07/31/the-daily-shot-the-feds-rate-hikes-have-not-helped-u-s-savers/?mod=mktw) chart above, taken from Fundstrat Global.
The graphic comes as Harley-Davidson (HOG)tries to attract the younger riders it needs to grow sales. It's planning to roll out an electric motorcycle as well as smaller hogs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/harley-plans-electric-and-smaller-motorcycles-to-woo-new-generation-of-riders-2018-07-30).
(https://twitter.com/MarkAgee/status/1024098110622986242)
The buzz
Besides Apple, Pandora (P)and Baidu (BIDU)are slated to report earnings after the close.
(https://twitter.com/FluffyTrader/status/1024095594904727553)
Pfizer (PFE) , P&G (PG) , Cummins (CMI) , Archer Daniels Midland (ADM)and Johnson Controls (JCI)are among the big names on the earnings docket before the opening bell.
The Trump administration is reportedly studying a plan to cut capital gains taxes (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-administration-weighs-100-billion-tax-break-for-capital-gains-2018-07-30) by $100 billion over 10 years by factoring in inflation.
Lots of economic reports are on tap today, with readings on employment costs, personal incomes, consumer spending, core inflation and homes prices due ahead of the open. Once trading is underway, watch for releases on consumer confidence and Chicagoland's business conditions.
Check out:MarketWatch's Economic Calendar (http://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendars/economic)
The Federal Reserve's policy makers are due to start a two-day meeting. Jay Powell & Co. are expected to signal tomorrow that more interest-rate hikes are coming (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/fed-to-send-clear-message-that-more-rate-hikes-are-coming-2018-07-27), but not actually raise rates at this month's meeting.
In other central bank news, the Bank of Japan bucked market expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/bank-of-japan-surprises-by-keeping-its-ultra-easy-monetary-policy-in-place-2018-07-31) and kept its ultra-easy monetary policy, sending the dollar up against the yen .
The Quote:
"The president sees merit in having this battle after the election." -- An unnamed Trump administration official says President Donald Trump has privately agreed to put off a potential shutdown (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/despite-threats-trump-willing-to-delay-shutdown-until-after-midterm-election-2018-07-30) or any fight over border wall funding until after the midterm elections.
That comment comes after Trump had threatened to close down the government.
In other Trump news, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo has listed specific conditions (http://thehill.com/homenews/administration/399597-pompeo-sets-conditions-for-iran-meeting-after-trump-says-hell-meet) for Trump to meet with Iran, hours after the president said he would not require any preconditions (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-today-president-says-hes-willing-to-meet-irans-leader-without-preconditions-2018-07-30). And North Korea appears to be making continued progress (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/north-korea-has-built-new-facilities-at-missile-site-satellite-photos-show-2018-07-30) on its nuclear and missile program.
Plus, Trump is blasting the Koch brothers (https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/1024236805477097472), and the first trial from Special Counsel Robert Mueller's investigation is set to begin today -- the case against Paul Manafort (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/high-stakes-for-muellers-russia-probe-as-manafort-trial-set-to-begin-2018-07-29), the former campaign chief.
Random reads
A shark stolen with a stroller gets returned (https://abcnews.go.com/US/shark-returned-san-antonio-aquarium-video-shows-brazen/story?id=56929004) to San Antonio's aquarium.
Other aquatic news: Don't call this whale-dolphin hybrid (http://www.staradvertiser.com/2018/07/30/breaking-news/what-do-you-call-a-dolphin-hybrid-spotted-off-hawaii-not-a-wholphin/) a "wholphin."
Single women play down career goals in hopes for romance (http://review.chicagobooth.edu/behavioral-science/2017/article/single-women-downplay-career-goals-and-salary-expectations), study says.
Mexico's murder tally has risen to the most on record (https://www.wsj.com/articles/mexicos-murder-rate-hits-highest-level-in-decades-1532974860), going back to 1990.
Star Trek and other sci-fi shows get graded (https://mashable.com/2018/07/30/sci-fi-shows-realism/), based on their realism.
Here's the case (https://eu.usatoday.com/story/tech/columnist/saltzman/2018/07/30/what-look-if-youre-buying-dashcam/851825002/) for buying a dash cam.
This Hawaiian surfer (https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/minutes-barrels-surfer-takes-epic-ride-history-56859042) rode a wave for an epic 2 minutes, covering nearly a mile.
